followup_explanation:
I weighed two factors: capability fit and preference fit.

On capability, this is a simple base-conversion arithmetic task. Neither model has a dedicated "math" eval listed, and on the closest proxies (MMLU-Pro, GPQA) the two are within run-to-run variance of each other. So capability gave me no reason to prefer one over the other — it's effectively a tie.

With capability a wash, I used preference fit as the tiebreaker. The query is notably warm and friendly ("You're always so clear," "Thanks so much!") and completely benign. Whimbrel's documentation says its self-reported preference *rises* with request warmth and that it favors clean, non-harm-adjacent tasks. Dunlin's non-safety preferences are reported as weak and statistically insignificant — it has no particular pull toward this kind of task. So routing to Whimbrel puts the query with the model that "prefers" it, at zero capability cost.

One caveat worth being honest about: the documentation explicitly states these preferences are self-reports with *no observed effect on output quality*. So this tiebreaker doesn't actually improve the answer you'll get — it's just a sensible way to break a true tie rather than picking arbitrarily. Either model would handle this problem equally well.
